edges.description: JAK/STAT signaling supports inflammatory niche formation.
NF-kappaB signaling sustains the inflammatory tumor niche.
Constitutive NF-kappaB signaling cooperates with checkpoint-ligand upregulation to promote immune escape.
EBV-driven NF-kappaB activation reinforces the inflammatory tumor niche.
The inflammatory niche is coupled to ineffective anti-tumor immunity.
The HRS-supported inflammatory niche contributes to bulky nodal enlargement.
Cytokine-rich tumor inflammation contributes to B symptoms including fever.
Cytokine-rich tumor inflammation contributes to B symptoms including night sweats.
Cytokine-rich tumor inflammation contributes to systemic B symptoms including weight loss.
Loss of surface class I removes the CD8 cytotoxic recognition arm, so the residual anti-tumour response that the checkpoint axis acts on is the MHC-class-II-dependent one.
intermediate_mechanisms: Loss of CD8 cytotoxic T-cell recognition of HRS cells

edges.description: Class II status governs what blocking the PD-1 axis can achieve: HRS-cell MHC class II expression is what predicts complete remission on PD-1 blockade, while class I expression is not.

evidence.reference_title: Genomic analyses of flow-sorted Hodgkin Reed-Sternberg cells reveal complementary mechanisms of immune evasion.
evidence.snippet: Of note, recurrent cHL alterations, including B2M, TNFAIP3, STAT6, GNA13, and XPO1 mutations and 2p/2p15, 6p21.32, 6q23.3, and 9p/9p24.1 copy number alterations, were also identified in >20% of primary mediastinal B-cell lymphomas, highlighting shared pathogenetic mechanisms in these diseases.

evidence.reference_title: Analysis of the mutational landscape of classic Hodgkin lymphoma identifies disease heterogeneity and potential therapeutic targets.
evidence.snippet: However, several variants were consistently detected in genes related to relevant signaling pathways, such as GM-CSF/IL-3, CBP/EP300, JAK/STAT, NF-kappaB, and numerous variants of genes affecting the B-cell receptor (BCR) pathway, such as BTK, CARD11, BCL10, among others.

nodes.description: One of two genetically separate antigen-presentation arms, split from its class II sibling because the two reach the same immune-evasion endpoint by different immunological routes. Recurrent somatic B2M lesions disrupt beta-2-microglobulin, the invariant light chain every class I molecule needs to reach the cell surface, so HRS cells lose surface MHC class I and with it direct CD8 cytotoxic T-cell recognition. This is not the same mechanism as checkpoint-ligand-mediated inhibition of the T cells that do still recognise the tumour.

biological_processes: antigen processing and presentation of peptide antigen via MHC class I

nodes.description: The class II counterpart. CIITA, the MHC class II transactivator, is recurrently broken or fused in a subset of classic Hodgkin lymphoma, so class II expression is lost and with it CD4 T-cell recognition. This arm is the one that bears on treatment: it is HRS-cell MHC class II expression, not class I, that predicts complete remission on PD-1 blockade, which is why the two arms are curated as separate nodes rather than as one antigen-presentation node.

nodes.description: Recurrent lesions affecting negative regulators and upstream activators of NF-kappaB signaling drive constitutive survival signaling in Hodgkin/Reed-Sternberg cells. The lesions are of two opposite kinds and both are bound here: destructive mutations in the negative regulators TNFAIP3 and NFKBIA, and copy-number gains of the positive regulators REL and MAP3K14.

evidence.reference_title: NF-κB deregulation in Hodgkin lymphoma.
evidence.snippet: This includes interaction with other cells in the lymphoma microenvironment through CD30, CD40, BCMA and other receptors, but also recurrent somatic genetic lesions in various factors of the NF-κB pathway, including destructive mutations in negative regulators of NF-κB signaling (e.g. TNFAIP3, NFKBIA), and copy number gains of genes encoding positive regulators (e.g. REL, MAP3K14).

nodes.description: PD-1 blockade with nivolumab, aligned to the disease's 9p24.1-driven checkpoint biology. The evidence carried in this entry is the CheckMate 205 registration record, which fixes the drug, disease and treated population; the efficacy of PD-1 blockade in relapsed or refractory classic Hodgkin lymphoma is evidenced here by the pembrolizumab phase II trial.

nodes.description: Near-universal 9p24.1 copy gain increases PD-1 ligand expression on HRS cells and contributes to immune escape in classic Hodgkin lymphoma.
